1.title: Pods and the Workload Resources
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Pods and the Workload Resources. It covers the exam area Application Design and Build. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. The Pod and the controllers that run it. Create them fast. Jobs in detail. Cron Jobs in detail. Stateful Sets in short. Self-healing basics. Practice with seven hands-on labs worth thirty-nine points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Application Design and Build (twenty percent). Practice in this module: seven labs, thirty-nine points, about forty-one minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: The Pod and the controllers that run it
1.text: The Pod and the controllers that run it. The figure shows this: Which controller creates which Pods. Exam tip: Read the kind in the task: every node is a Daemon Set, run once is a Job, run on a schedule is a Cron Job.

1.title: The Pod and the controllers that run it, continued
1.text: The Pod and the controllers that run it. A Pod is the smallest unit you deploy: one or more containers that share a network address and volumes. You almost never run a bare Pod in real life, because nobody restarts it on another node if the node dies. You put a controller in front of it: the controller creates Pods from a template and keeps the right number running.

1.title: The Pod and the controllers that run it, continued
1.text: The Pod and the controllers that run it. Pod. Use it for: one-off tests, debugging. Pod names: the name you give. Key facts: no replacement if the node fails. Deployment. Use it for: stateless apps. Pod names: name- hash - id. Key facts: owns Replica Sets; rolling updates and rollbacks (Module five). Replica Set. Use it for: keeps N Pods running. Pod names: name- id. Key facts: you rarely create it: a Deployment does. Daemon Set. Use it for: one Pod per node (agents, log shippers). Pod names: name- id. Key facts: ignores replicas; needs tolerations for tainted nodes.

1.title: The Pod and the controllers that run it, continued
1.text: The Pod and the controllers that run it. Stateful Set. Use it for: apps that need a stable identity or storage. Pod names: name-zero, name-one,... Key facts: governing Service (headless); ordered start. Job. Use it for: run to completion once. Pod names: name- id. Key facts: completions, parallelism, backoff Limit; restart Policy is Never or On Failure. Cron Job. Use it for: Jobs on a schedule. Pod names: Job per run. Key facts: cron schedule; suspend pauses it. How to choose. Ask three questions. Does it run forever or finish? (forever: Deployment, Daemon Set, Stateful Set; finishes: Job, Cron Job.) Does it need one copy per node? (Daemon Set.) Does each copy need its own name and disk? (Stateful Set; otherwise Deployment.).

1.title: Create them fast
1.text: Create them fast. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A Daemon Set has no create command: generate a Deployment with the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml, change the kind and delete replicas and strategy.

1.title: Create them fast, continued
1.text: Create them fast. A Daemon Set and a Stateful Set have no create command. Generate a Deployment with the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml, change kind, delete replicas and strategy (a Daemon Set has neither), and add what is missing. A Stateful Set also needs service Name and a headless Service. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create them fast, continued
1.text: Create them fast. Imperative commands that change a controller: kube control scale deployment api the replicas flag set to five, kube control set image deployment api engine X engine X stable alpine, kube control set env deployment api mode prod, kube control label, kube control annotate, kube control patch, kube control edit.

1.title: Jobs in detail
1.text: Jobs in detail. completions. Meaning: how many Pods must finish successfully. Default: one. parallelism. Meaning: how many Pods run at the same time. Default: one. backoff Limit. Meaning: retries before the Job is marked failed. Default: six. active Deadline Seconds. Meaning: total time limit for the whole Job. Default: none. ttl Seconds After Finished. Meaning: delete the finished Job (and its Pods) after this many seconds. Default: never. template dot spec dot restart Policy. Meaning: must be Never or On Failure. Default: (none: required). Exam tip: A Job's restart Policy must be Never or On Failure; Always is rejected.

1.title: Jobs in detail, continued
1.text: Jobs in detail. restart Policy Always (the Pod default) is rejected in a Job: that is a classic "fix the manifest" task. With On Failure the same Pod restarts its container; with Never a failed Pod stays and a new Pod is created (that is why backoff Limit counts Pods). To wait for completion: kube control wait the for flag set to condition complete job slash batch the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. To read the output: kube control logs job slash batch.

1.title: CronJobs in detail
1.text: Cron Jobs in detail. The schedule has five fields: minute hour day of month month day of week. or five is every five minutes; zero two one is two:zero every Monday. The schedule is evaluated in the controller's time zone unless you set time Zone. Exam tip: kube control create job the from flag set to cronjob or name runs a Cron Job's work right now.

1.title: CronJobs in detail, continued
1.text: Cron Jobs in detail. concurrency Policy. Allow (default), Forbid (skip a run if the last one is still running), Replace (stop the old run and start the new one). successful Jobs History Limit or failed Jobs History Limit. how many finished Jobs to keep (defaults three and one). starting Deadline Seconds. how late a missed run may still start. suspend. true stops new runs without deleting the Cron Job. job Template. the Job (with its Pod template) that each run creates.

1.title: StatefulSets in short
1.text: Stateful Sets in short. A Stateful Set gives each Pod a stable name ( db-zero, db-one ), starts them in order, and with volume Claim Templates gives each its own Persistent Volume Claim (Module four). A headless Service ( cluster I P None ) gives each Pod its own D N S name: db-zero dot db. namespace dot svc dot cluster dot local. Set service Name to that Service. Deleting a Stateful Set does not delete its P V Cs.

1.title: Self-healing basics
1.text: Self-healing basics. A Pod's restart Policy ( Always, On Failure, Never ) tells the kubelet when to restart a failed container. Controllers set what they need; a bare Pod defaults to Always. A Deployment replaces Pods that disappear; a Job replaces Pods that fail (up to backoff Limit ); a Daemon Set replaces a missing node Pod. Delete a Pod owned by a controller and a new one appears: to stop it, delete the controller.

1.title: Self-healing basics, continued
1.text: Self-healing basics. Exam tip. Read the kind in the task. "Run on every node" is a Daemon Set, "run once and finish" is a Job, "run every night" is a Cron Job. The wrong kind scores zero even if the container runs. Exam tip. kube control create job the from flag set to cronjob or name job starts a Cron Job's work now; tasks ask for it.

1.title: Lab 2.1: pod spec
1.text: Lab two point one: pod spec. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a Pod named web with the image engine X alpine, the labels app web and tier frontend, the environment variable mode prod, and the container port eighty declared. Wait until it is Running. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 2.1: pod spec, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n wl run web the image flag set to engine X alpine the labels flag set to app web,tier frontend the env flag set to mode prod the port flag set, and so on. Then kube control dash n wl wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 2.2: deployment template label
1.text: Lab two point two: deployment template label. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a Deployment named api with the image engine X alpine and three replicas. Then add the label tier backend to the Pods that the Deployment creates (that is, to the Pod template), so that kube control get pods dash l tier backend lists three Ready Pods. Wait for the rollout to finish. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 2.2: deployment template label, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n wl create deployment api the image flag set to engine X alpine the replicas flag set to three. Then kube control dash n wl patch deployment api dash p spec template metadata labels tier backend. Then kube control dash n wl rollout status deployment api the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n wl get pods dash l tier backend. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.3: job completions
2.text: Lab two point three: job completions. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a Job named batch with the image busy box one dot thirty-six that runs sh dash c echo done. It must run four Pods to completion in total, two at a time ( completions four, parallelism two ), and be retried at most two times on failure ( backoff Limit two ). Wait until the Job is complete. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.3: job completions, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n wl create job batch the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml then the command sh dash c, and so on. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f slash temp slash batch dot yaml. Then kube control dash n wl wait the for flag set to condition complete job slash batch the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.4: cronjob settings
2.text: Lab two point four: cronjob settings. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a Cron Job named tick with the image busy box one dot thirty-six that runs date every five minutes. It must not start a run while the previous one is still running ( concurrency Policy Forbid ), and keep the last two successful and the last one failed Jobs. Then start one run now, by creating a Job named tick manual from the Cron Job, and wait until that Job is complete. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.4: cronjob settings, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n wl create cronjob tick the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the schedule flag set to or five then the command date. Then kube control dash n wl patch cronjob tick dash p spec concurrency Policy Forbid, successful Jobs History Limit two, failed Jobs History Limit one. Then kube control dash n wl create job tick manual the from flag set to cronjob slash tick. Then kube control dash n wl wait the for flag set to condition complete job slash tick manual the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.5: daemonset all nodes
2.text: Lab two point five: daemonset all nodes. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a Daemon Set named agent with the image busy box one dot thirty-six that runs sleep three thousand six hundred. It must run one Pod on every node of the cluster, including the control plane node (which has a No Schedule taint). Wait until all its Pods are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.5: daemonset all nodes, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n wl create deployment agent the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml then the command sleep three thousand, and so on. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f slash temp slash ds dot yaml. Then kube control dash n wl rollout status daemonset agent the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n wl get pods dash o wide. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.6: fix job manifest
2.text: Lab two point six: fix job manifest. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The file about slash work slash report job dot yaml defines the Job report in the namespace wl, but kube control apply dash f rejects it. Fix the file without changing the Job name, the image or the command, create the Job, and wait until it is complete. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.6: fix job manifest, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control apply dash f about slash work slash report job dot yaml. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash report job dot yaml. Then kube control dash n wl wait the for flag set to condition complete job slash report the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.7: statefulset headless
2.text: Lab two point seven: statefulset headless. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a headless Service named db (port eighty, selecting Pods with the label app db ) and a Stateful Set named db with two replicas of the image engine X alpine, whose service Name is db and whose Pods carry the label app db. Wait until the Pods db-zero and db-one are Ready. The name db-zero dot db dot wl dot svc dot cluster dot local must answer on port eighty from inside the cluster. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.7: statefulset headless, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n wl apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.7: statefulset headless, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab two point seven: statefulset headless, Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version apps slash version one. Then kind Stateful Set. Then metadata name db. Then spec. Then service Name db. Then replicas two. Then selector match Labels app db. Then template. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which workload resource runs one Pod on every node? Answer: A Daemon Set. Question two. Which restart Policy values are allowed in a Job's Pod template? Answer: Never or On Failure. Question three. What do completions and parallelism mean in a Job? Answer: Completions is how many Pods must succeed in total; parallelism is how many run at the same time.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does concurrency Policy Forbid do on a Cron Job? Answer: It skips a new run while the previous run is still running. Question five. Which command starts a Cron Job's work immediately? Answer: kube control create job name the from flag set to cronjob or cronjob. Question six. What does a Stateful Set's service Name point to? Answer: A headless Service ( cluster I P None ) that gives the Pods stable D N S names.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. How do you make a Daemon Set Pod run on the tainted control plane node? Answer: Add a toleration for the node role dot Kubernetes dot io slash control plane No Schedule taint. Question eight. Why use a Deployment instead of a bare Pod? Answer: The controller replaces Pods that fail or disappear and provides rolling updates; a bare Pod is not replaced.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Choose: forever: Deployment; per node: Daemon Set; stable identity: Stateful Set; once: Job; schedule: Cron Job. Fast create: run, create deployment, create job, create cronjob; the from flag set to cronjob slash x. No create command: Daemon Set, Stateful Set: generate a Deployment yamel and edit. Job: completions, parallelism, backoff Limit, restart Policy Never or On Failure. Cron Job: five-field schedule, concurrency Policy, history limits, suspend. Stateful Set: name-zero, headless Service, service Name. Daemon Set: no replicas; tolerate the control plane taint to reach all nodes.
